neighbours.label: the comma that closes a second-person wish-style hypothetical (If you could ..., If you had to ...), as opposed to the comma after a real condition or a when-clause, including a real 'could' or 'had to'
fire: If you could have dinner with anyone from history, who would it be?
If you had to eat one food forever, what would you choose?
If you could visit any country next year, where would you go?
If you had to leave your home tonight, what would you take?
If you could change one thing about your town, what would it be?
If you had to pick one song to keep, which would it be?
If you could learn any language overnight, which one would you pick?
If you could go back and relive one day, which day would it be?
quiet: If you have dinner with your family tonight, tell them the news.
If you eat this food too often, you will get sick.
If you visit that country next year, bring a warm coat.
When you leave your home tonight, lock the back door.
If you had to pay for parking last week, keep the receipt.
When you pick a song to keep, write it on the list.
If you could send the form by Friday, please do.
When you go back to the office, call the client.

short: comma after an 'if you could / had to' hypothetical
notes: Card: scattered function words (' and', ',', ' of', '-', ' then', ' but'). Probes: 'If you had to give up one of your senses,' 0.72, 'If you could live anywhere in the world,' 0.58, 'If you had to part with a piece of your body,' 0.55; 'If you lost one of your senses,' 0.23, 'If you were stuck on an island,' 0.11, 'When you were stuck' 0.08. A broader reading (the join before a wh-word) was uneven: 'who will drive and' 0.37, 'how the engine works and' 0.16, 'who owns the land and' 0.10. So only the hypothetical comma is claimed, and it covers a small part of the pole. Peak is on the comma, before the question starts ('..., I would be surprised' scored the same 0.58), so no claim is made about what comes next, and the near misses differ before it. Other hypotheticals were weak ('If you were stuck' 0.11, 'If you lost' 0.23).
